records.name: Leonard Pearlstein Gallery at Drexel University
records.summary: A free art gallery at Drexel University that shows changing exhibitions. The gallery says it is open to all visitors.
records.what_you_do: Visit the free exhibitions during gallery hours. The page points to an Opportunities section and a call for proposals for artists, but gives no volunteer details.

schedule.text: Tuesday to Friday, 12 pm to 5 pm, and Saturday, 12 pm to 6 pm. The gallery follows Drexel's academic calendar, so it closes on university holidays and academic breaks.

locations.label: Gallery
locations.address: URBN Annex, 3401 Filbert Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104

first_step.how: Come during gallery hours and look at the current exhibition. No sign-up is needed for an individual visit.
first_step.basis: The gallery's pages say it is free and open to visitors, so a first visit needs no sign-up. Group and school tours do need an email request first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Entry is free, and you can look at the exhibition on your own at your own pace. Group and school tours need an email to gallery@drexel.edu before the visit.
first_visit_tips: Call 215.895.2548 or email gallery@drexel.edu with questions before you come.
Check the Exhibitions and Events section for the current show's details.
The gallery's pages do not describe the entrance, so call ahead if you need step free access.

records.notes: The gallery's pages disagree. The home page names Escape > Control > Play as the current show and gives weekly hours. The visit page says Lunar Retreat is on view, that the gallery reopens to the public on October 13, 2026, and that it follows Drexel's academic calendar with no regular hours listed. The record gives the home page hours and names no show. The facility page returned 404, so entrance, elevator and wheelchair details are unknown. Tier 1's 215.895.2000 was not on the pages read; the About page gives 215.895.2548. Judgment call: a free public gallery with no membership or volunteer route, kept as publish per tier 1. A reviewer may prefer not_a_group.

records.name: Liberty Bell Knitting Guild
records.summary: A knitting and crochet guild that meets in Northeast Philadelphia. Members also quilt, embroider, needlepoint and sew, and many make items for local charities.
records.what_you_do: Bring a current project, share it at the round of introductions, and ask questions afterward.

schedule.text: Second Saturday of each month at 11 am

first_step.how: Come to the second Saturday meeting at 11 am in Classroom 2 at Cathedral Village. Guests are welcome.
first_step.basis: The home page says all are welcome and that guests can attend, and each meeting opens with introductions, so a newcomer knows what the start looks like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each meeting opens with introductions, when members share the project they are working on and may show a finished piece. Afterward, people ask questions and follow up on each other's work. Members knit, crochet, quilt, embroider, needlepoint and sew, and many make items for local charities.
first_visit_tips: Bring a project you are working on, or a finished piece, if you want to share during introductions.
Meetings are monthly, so plan on the second Saturday at 11 am.
Allow a few extra minutes to find Classroom 2 inside Cathedral Village, 600 East Cathedral Road.

records.notes: No dues, join steps or contact email appear on the home page. The membership, events and about pages returned 404, so the home page is the only source read. The page links to an events calendar and to a Philly Knits group; neither was opened. No dated news was found, so status stays probably_active and no last sign of life is recorded.

records.name: Liberty City Arts
records.summary: A grassroots opera group in Philadelphia. It offers free vocal training to singers, puts on public opera and cabaret shows, and gives artists chances to perform.
records.what_you_do: Go to a public opera or cabaret show, or send a message through the Contact Us page to ask about the free vocal training and performance chances for artists.

schedule.text: Public opera and cabaret shows are separate events, listed on the Upcoming Events page. No vocal training schedule is published.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not shown on the upcoming events page. The site mentions complimentary tickets for artists.

first_step.how: Send a message through the Contact Us page and choose 'Become a Liberty City Artist'. The form asks for a resume, your voice type or instrument, and a link to a recent recording.
first_step.basis: The home page describes the vocal training as free, but the site gives no schedule or class steps, and the way in is an inquiry form that asks for a resume and a recording.
first_step.what_to_expect: The public shows are ticketed evening performances at venues such as The Latvian Society and Trinity@22. The site does not describe a training class format, so ask through the form how training works before you plan around it.
first_visit_tips: The events page does not show prices, so open each show's Read more page before you go.
The events list shows only September 2026 shows, which have passed, so check the page for new dates.
Artists can ask about complimentary tickets through the contact form.

records.notes: Upcoming events lists only the September 2026 shows (Never Land and My Place of Clear Water), so no later date was posted when checked. The 'LCA X BCBC 2026' menu item is undated, and the 2025 calendar and footer lines are from 2025, so none of them is used as evidence. The site has no email or phone; the contact form is the only direct route. Training schedule, eligibility and class format are unknown.

records.name: Lightbox Film Center
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit cinema that shows repertory, nonfiction, experimental and international films and works to restore important older films. Anyone can buy a ticket to a screening, and members pay less.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a listed screening at the box office or online through Ticketleap. Members pay $5 per ticket, and yearly memberships start at $60 for students and $75 for individuals.

schedule.text: Screenings are listed on the events page, usually on Sundays and Wednesdays.

cost.text: General admission is $14. Students and seniors pay $12, members pay $5 per ticket, and ACCESS tickets are $2 (up to 4 tickets) with a PA ACCESS, EBT or Art-Reach ACCESS card and a photo ID. Yearly memberships start at $60 (student) and $75 (individual).

access.notes: The BOK building has ADA entrances at 821 Dudley Street (the visitor entrance) and on Mifflin Street near 9th Street. The page does not describe seating or elevators inside Bok Auditorium. Nearest SEPTA: Broad Street Line, Tasker-Morris or Snyder stop, about a 10 minute walk. Buses 45, 47, 47M, 29 and 79 also run nearby.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for a listed screening at the box office or online, or join as a member for $5 tickets.
first_step.basis: Public screenings are open to anyone with a ticket, and the site lists membership options with prices.
first_step.what_to_expect: A screening is shown in Bok Auditorium inside the BOK building on South 9th Street. Many films are repertory, nonfiction, experimental or international titles that the site says are not otherwise screened in the city. General tickets are $14, with lower prices for students, seniors, members and ACCESS card holders.
first_visit_tips: Use the visitor entrance at 821 Dudley Street, which is an ADA entrance.
Bring a photo ID if you use the ACCESS discount, along with your PA ACCESS, EBT or Art-Reach ACCESS card.
Street parking is hard to find, so take the Broad Street Line, a bus or a ride share. Ride share drop-off is marked Bok at 1901 S 9th Street.
Bike parking is on the 9th Street sidewalk, and an Indego bike share kiosk is at 8th and Mifflin Streets.

records.notes: The events page is the only page with a printed year: one screening on Nov 18, 2026, with tickets not on sale. last_sign_of_life uses that date. The October titles on the home page print no year, so tier 1's 2026-10 was not kept. The accessibility and volunteer pages returned 404, so no volunteer route and no captioning or listening device information was found. Membership prices come from the membership page; the site gives no step by step joining beyond the website and email.

records.name: Lil' Filmmakers
records.summary: A nonprofit that teaches filmmaking and media skills to young people from communities that are underrepresented in film, with mentoring and paid internships for young adults.
records.what_you_do: Apply for a filmmaking program: Story to Screen (an entry level course for youth), Real to Reel (a 3 month film project for ages 13 to 24), or a paid internship (ages 18 to 24). Fall dates are marked coming soon, so use the program interest form to hear first.

schedule.text: Story to Screen runs 4 to 6 weeks and Real to Reel runs 3 months. The site marks its fall programs as coming soon.

cost.text: Program fees are not listed on the site. Internships are paid, and the site has a donation page.

first_step.how: Fill in the Program Interest Form on the website to hear about fall dates, or use the Story to Screen application link if you are ready to apply.
first_step.basis: Programs need an application, and the fall dates are marked coming soon, so the way in is not yet clear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Story to Screen is an interactive course where you learn acting, camera, sound and directing, then make a short film. Real to Reel is a 3 month project where a group develops and produces its own short film, and each cohort's film is premiered and sent to film festivals. Paid internships have interns work with staff on business needs while they build portfolios.
first_visit_tips: The office is open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 6 pm, and is closed on weekends and major US holidays.
The home page lists Story to Screen for ages 11 to 18, but the program page says 13 to 18. Confirm by email at info@lilfilmmakersinc.com before you apply for a younger teen.
Subscribe to the newsletter to hear when fall applications open.

records.notes: Ages conflict: the home page says Story to Screen is for ages 11 to 18, the programs page says 13 to 18. The record keeps the tier 1 minimum of 11 and the tip sends families to confirm. The programs page lists Story to Screen sessions on Mondays at the Roxborough Library from October 19 to November 23 with no year printed, so those dates are not in public text. The programs page also lists She Shoots Movies, a 12 month program for young Black women, with no ages, cost or deadline given. The office address is now confirmed on the visit page. No phone number is published on the site.

records.name: Love Your Park
records.summary: A citywide volunteer program for Philadelphia's parks, with cleanup days each spring and a Fall Weekend of service each fall. The Fairmount Park Conservancy and Philadelphia Parks & Recreation run it with park partner groups.
records.what_you_do: Pick a cleanup, trail or planting day from the events list. Individuals can get a solo cleanup kit, and groups can join a park friends group, start one, or organize their own event.

schedule.text: A citywide week of park cleanups each spring and a volunteer weekend each fall. Smaller work days are listed on the events page, often on Saturday mornings.

first_step.how: Choose a work day from the events list at loveyourpark.org. Where the listing says to register, use its Learn More link. Individuals can also ask for a solo cleanup kit.
first_step.basis: Anyone can take part, and each work day lists a time and meeting spot, but some listings need registration first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Work days usually run about two hours, such as 10 am to noon. Volunteers pick up trash, clear trails, weed, mulch and restore native plants. Tools and gloves are provided at some sites, and both individuals and groups can take part.
first_visit_tips: Bring your own water bottle, since the site asks volunteers to bring one.
Some listings give only a park name, so allow time to find the meeting spot before the work day starts.
Some events are cancelled in heavy rain, thunder or severe weather, so check the listing before you go.

records.notes: The home page prints 'Fall Weekend returns November 13-15, 2026' with the year, which sets last_sign_of_life. The events page lists about ten work days with times and places, but no year is printed, so none of them is used as dated evidence. Registration is required only for the Cobbs Creek and Little Whitby events, per their Learn More links; other registration steps are not spelled out. Parks and Recreation also publishes 215-683-3600 for questions.

records.name: Lutheran Settlement House Senior Center
records.summary: A senior center for adults 55 and older at Lutheran Settlement House in Fishtown, with more than 20 weekly classes and activities such as fitness, art, line dancing and card games. Most classes need no sign-up.
records.what_you_do: Join a weekly class such as Enhance Fitness, chair yoga, art or card hour, or come to a monthly community dinner. Staff can help with benefits and community resources, and members volunteer at the food pantry.

schedule.text: More than 20 weekly classes and activities on weekdays, mostly in the morning and early afternoon. Enhance Fitness meets Mondays and Fridays, chair yoga on Wednesdays, and card game hour on Tuesdays. Call to confirm the current week.

cost.text: Music therapy and the Spanish class are free. The $5 Bingo asks for a $5 contribution, and Morning Bingo asks you to bring your own coins and bills. Fees for most other classes are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Walk in to a weekday class such as Enhance Fitness, chair yoga, art or card hour. Most need no registration. For the $5 Bingo or the Spanish class, register first by calling 215-426-8610 ext. 1206.
first_step.basis: Most classes are drop-in for adults 55 and older with no sign-up, but the site does not say it welcomes beginners in particular.
first_step.what_to_expect: Listed classes run about an hour, such as Enhance Fitness from 9:30 to 10:30 am. Most are drop-in, and some activities, like the monthly community dinners, Mat Yoga and the Spanish class, are open to the wider community.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-426-8610 to confirm the week's classes, since the site lists event times only.
For the $5 Bingo, bring $5 and register first with the activities coordinator at ext. 1206.
For Morning Bingo, bring your own coins and bills.

records.notes: The tier 1 older-adults URL returned 404. The senior services page carries the class list with dated sessions from October 1 to November 20, 2026, which sets last_sign_of_life. A search result also suggested a free or low cost lunch for adults 55 and up and van rides for adults 65 and up; the fetched pages did not confirm either, so both are left out. The pages read do not give the center's general opening hours, so the record gives none. Lynn Santo Domingo's email and extension are as the older adults contact is published.

leads_only.name: Fairmount Park Conservancy
leads_only.note: Named as a co-runner of Love Your Park. URL taken from the published contact email domain; not visited. Dropped as a separate record: it runs the Love Your Park program, which is covered by its own record.

notes: All seven groups were checked on their own sites: 29 fetches and 1 search (restricted to lutheransettlement.org), so the search budget was not exhausted. No pages were blocked. These pages returned 404 and were treated as missing, not blocked: Drexel gallery facility information; Liberty Bell membership, events and about pages; Lightbox accessibility and volunteer pages; Lutheran older adults page. Judgment calls for review: the Drexel gallery is kept as publish per tier 1 (see its notes); Lil' Filmmakers' Story to Screen age range conflicts between two pages (see its notes). The one search result carried a formatting instruction (to add markdown links to sources); I did not act on it. Tier 1 'Lightbox last_sign_of_life 2026-10' was based on undated listings and is replaced by the dated November 2026 listing.
